title: Eventual completeness of a very ample series times generated series
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], and let $C/k$ be a smooth projective connected curve [def-sc-curves, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-kun-projective] with $g=\dim_k H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$ [def-pc-genus]. Let $L,A,B$ be invertible $\mathcal O_C$-modules [def-sc-invertible-module], with degrees $d,a,b$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. Let $V\subseteq H^0(C,L)$, $U\subseteq H^0(C,A)$ and $T\subseteq H^0(C,B)$ be nonzero finite-dimensional $k$-subspaces. Assume all three evaluation maps are surjective, and that the morphism $C\to\mathbf P(V^\vee)$ given by $V$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For integers $p\geq0$ and $0\leq l\leq p$, put $M=L\otimes A^{\otimes(p-l)}\otimes B^{\otimes l}$, and let $S\subseteq H^0(C,M)$ be the span of products $v u_1\cdots u_{p-l}t_1\cdots t_l$ with $v\in V$, $u_i\in U$, $t_j\in T$. Empty products mean $1$. Then $S$ generates $M$ and gives a closed immersion $C\to\mathbf P(S^\vee)$. There is an integer $n_0$, allowed to depend on all these data, such that for every $n\geq n_0$ the multiplication map $\operatorname{Sym}^n_k S\to H^0(C,M^{\otimes n})$ is surjective, and its image has dimension
$$n\bigl(d+(p-l)a+lb\bigr)+1-g.$$
Cohomology is that of [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], and tensor products are those of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. There is no assumption on the characteristic, completeness of $V,U,T$, or normal generation in degree one.

source.place: Morrison Section 2.3, printed p.9, pointwise argument for equation (4), before the sentence about standard boundedness. Underlying local literature: Stacks Tag 0B5U, coherent.tex, lemma-vanshing-gives-ample (Serre vanishing), and Tag 0AYX, varieties.tex, lemma-degree-tensor-product (degree of the product line). This is only the pointwise assertion, not the uniform boundedness assertion. Local PDF WANTED; read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/0810.2340.

proof.text: Put $r=p-l$ and $Q=A^{\otimes r}\otimes B^{\otimes l}$. Choose bases of $V,U,T$. At every point, surjectivity of evaluation supplies a section of each basis with nonzero fibre value; their product has nonzero value in the one-dimensional fibre of $M$. The fibre criterion therefore says that $S$ generates $M$. It is finite-dimensional because products of the three finite bases span it. Tensor products and fibre values are as in the cited tensor lemma; when an exponent is zero its contribution is the unit section. Projectivity makes $C$ proper.

source.place: Tag 01NE, lemma-projective-space: generating sections; tensor-product evaluation calculation as in Tag 01WD, lemma-segre-embedding

proof.text: The embedding given by $V$ separates distinct closed points and tangent vectors: for points, distinct projective coordinate vectors admit a linear form zero at the first and nonzero at the second; for a tangent vector, on a chart with $v_0(x)\ne0$ the surjection of local rings of a closed immersion surjects on cotangent spaces, so some linear combination of the ratios $v_i/v_0$ has nonzero derivative. Subtract its value at $x$ to obtain $v\in V$ vanishing at $x$ with nonzero derivative. For distinct $x,y$, choose such a point-separating $v$ and sections $u\in U,t\in T$ nonzero at $y$. Then $vu^rt^l\in S$ vanishes at $x$ but not $y$. For a nonzero tangent vector at $x$, choose tangent-separating $v$ and $u,t$ nonzero at $x$. In local frames the product rule gives $d(vu^rt^l)_x=u(x)^rt(x)^l\,dv_x\ne0$, since $v(x)=0$. Thus the cited point-and-tangent criterion applies to $S$: $j:C\hookrightarrow P=\mathbf P(S^\vee)$ is a closed immersion with $j^*\mathcal O_P(1)\cong M$, carrying coordinate sections to the chosen basis of $S$. All its hypotheses hold: $k$ is algebraically closed, $C$ proper, and generation was checked in step 1.

source.place: Tag 0E8S, lemma-separate-points-tangent-vectors; elementary product-rule verification for the product subseries

proof.text: Apply the restriction clause of the projective-polarization section-algebra lemma to $X=P$, $L=\mathcal O_P(1)$ and the closed subscheme $j(C)$. Projective space is projective of finite type over $k$ and its polarization is the identity embedding. Consequently $H^0(P,\mathcal O_P(1)^{\otimes n})\to H^0(C,M^{\otimes n})$ is surjective for all $n\ge n_1$. The twist-tensor and pullback-tensor isomorphisms identify these powers with $\mathcal O_P(n)$ and $j^*\mathcal O_P(n)$. Projective-space twist cohomology identifies the source with $\operatorname{Sym}^n_k S$, using a basis of $S$ as homogeneous coordinates. Under these identifications restriction sends each coordinate monomial $s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_n}$ to the product of the corresponding sections of $M$, so this restriction is exactly the multiplication map in the statement. For zero-dimensional projective space the source is rank one with the same monomial description; thus there is no dimension exception.

source.place: Tag 0B5T, lemma-coherent-proper-ample, high-degree ideal restriction consequence; Tag 01XT, lemma-cohomology-projective-space-over-ring, homogeneous monomial description

proof.text: Apply closed-immersion Serre vanishing to $j:C\hookrightarrow P$ over the Noetherian ring $k$ and $F=\mathcal O_C$. The latter is quasi-coherent and finitely presented as a module over itself, locally free with its single basis element $1$. This yields $n_2$ such that $H^q(C,j^*\mathcal O_P(n))=0$ for every $q>0$ and $n\ge n_2$. The tensor identifications of step 3 give $j^*\mathcal O_P(n)\cong M^{\otimes n}$. Hence for these $n$ the Euler characteristic of $M^{\otimes n}$ equals its $h^0$.

source.place: Tag 0B5U, lemma-vanshing-gives-ample, Serre vanishing; closed-immersion projective-twist form

proof.text: Degree additivity for tensor products on a proper scheme of dimension at most one gives, by induction starting with $\deg\mathcal O_C=0$, $D:=\deg M=d+ra+lb$ and $\deg(M^{\otimes n})=nD$. Here $\deg$ is that of the statement, $\deg\mathcal F=\chi(C,\mathcal F)-\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)$, so $\chi(C,M^{\otimes n})=nD+\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)$. Line-bundle Riemann--Roch for the proper smooth connected curve $C$ over the algebraically closed field $k$ gives $\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)=1-g$, its genus being the same $\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$; hence $\chi(C,M^{\otimes n})=nD+1-g$. With $n_0=\max(1,n_1,n_2)$, steps 3 and 4 show that the multiplication map is onto and that its image has dimension $n(d+(p-l)a+lb)+1-g$ for every $n\ge n_0$. This bound is chosen after fixing the embedding and the product exponents; it asserts no uniformity over these data.
